Use `snl library rename` to change the identity of one Library while preserving structured reference closure.

### Availability
This Entry is a normative product contract. The command is implemented only when its canonical path appears in machine-readable `snl --help`; absence means planned and unavailable, never silently emulated through a different command.


### Command path
`library/rename` is the canonical transport-neutral command. The intended shell spelling is `snl library rename`. Current availability is advertised by machine-readable `snl --help`; an Agent/MCP adapter submits the same operation object instead of reconstructing shell text.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"library/rename","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{"id":"<exact-id>","to":"<new-id>","expectedRevision":"<opaque>","checkedDigest":"<opaque>","expectedWorkspaceRevision":"<opaque>","dryRun":false}}
```
Every adapter accepts exactly this semantic request. Unknown argument keys are rejected. The CLI accepts `--root` and `--json` globally and emits one complete JSON document followed by a newline. Destination collision or stale plan is a conflict with no partial rewrite.

### Success result
A successful call exits `0` and returns `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"library/rename","data":{},"diagnostics":[]}`. `data` contains the deterministic rewrite plan, affected files/identities, `checkedDigest`, and `expectedWorkspaceRevision` during dry-run; apply additionally returns renamed canonical readback.

### Failure and exit semantics
Domain rejection (invalid data, not-found, conflict, or validation errors) exits `1`. Invocation, input I/O, unsupported workspace/schema, lock acquisition, and runtime failures exit `2`. Failure stdout under `--json` is exactly one `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"library/rename","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","details":{},"retryable":false}}`; no stack trace or prose contaminates stdout.

### State and concurrency
Dry-run is read-only and returns `checkedDigest` plus `expectedWorkspaceRevision`. Apply requires both tokens and the source revision, rederives the exact reviewed multi-entity rewrite plan under the shared lock, rejects any drift, updates all schema-owned references atomically, and validates projected state before publication. Revisions, cursors, checked digests, and workspace revisions are opaque tokens. After success, canonical readback and whole-workspace validation must observe the published state.
